front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** ([AGENCY ADDRESS], Maryland) operates its **Community Living – Group Home** service. The service is delivered under the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) Community Pathways Waiver and under a community residential services license issued under COMAR 10.22.

The manual does four things:

1. **Puts the required written policies in one place.** COMAR 10.22.02.10 requires a licensee to have written policies and procedures. This manual covers health and safety, fundamental rights, choice, confidentiality, grievances, nondiscrimination, incident reporting, medication administration, behavior safeguards, finances, infection control, and emergency and disaster planning.
2. **Gives staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers one standard to follow.** COMAR 10.22.02.10C requires each of them to know and implement every policy.
3. **Protects the people we support.** The manual is built around each person's rights, choices, health, safety and Individual Plan (IP). It also reflects the HCBS settings requirements (42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)) and the Community Settings Rule.
4. **Supports licensing and review.** DDA and the Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ) review this manual against the official policy checklist described in the Regulatory Framework section. The manual is organized so a reviewer can find the policy behind every checklist item.

**This manual is a template that must be customized before use.** Replace every bracketed placeholder, such as [AGENCY NAME], [ADMINISTRATIVE HEAD], [ADDRESS] and [PHONE], with the agency's actual information. Where a policy describes a practice the agency does not follow, change the practice or change the policy. A policy the agency does not actually follow is a compliance risk.

## How to Use This Manual

**Who must use it.** All staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers of [AGENCY NAME] must know and implement every policy in this manual (COMAR 10.22.02.10C). The governing body and administrative head use it to oversee compliance.

**How it is organized.** The policy sections follow the numbering and order of the official DDA policy checklist (DH Form DD.APP.1.1, 02/18): items A(1)–A(19), B(1)–B(7), C, D, and the Nursing items. Each policy carries the checklist item ID it satisfies, so a reviewer can match each box on the form to a page.

**Appendix A is the crosswalk.** Appendix A lists every official checklist item, with its exact wording, and names the policy and page that satisfies it. Use it to:
- prepare the checklist for submission (marking Present Yes/No/N/A);
- confirm that nothing was missed after you edit a policy;
- answer a surveyor who asks where an item is addressed.

The form has no numbers for its seven Nursing items. Appendix A labels them **Nursing-1 through Nursing-7**, in the order the form lists them. These items cite specific Medication Training and Technical Procedures (MTTP) sections, so the medication policies reference those sections.

**Steps to put the manual into service**

1. **Customize it.** Replace all [AGENCY NAME] and other bracketed placeholders. Add local details, such as the number of homes, licensed capacity, names and contact numbers, and local emergency management contacts.
2. **Check it against the Program Service Plan (PSP), the QA plan and the IPs.** Policies must match the DDA-approved PSP and QA plan, and staff must follow the approved PSP (COMAR 10.22.02.09D).
3. **Have the governing body adopt it.** The governing body is legally responsible for overseeing all programs and for compliance (COMAR 10.22.02.02A(2)–(3)). Its bylaws must cover policy approval (COMAR 10.22.02.08). Record the adoption in the minutes and fill in the adoption block below.
4. **Train staff on it.** Training must be completed and documented before staff begin independent duties and again whenever policies change. Staff training topics and timelines under COMAR 10.22.02.11C and D are tracked on the DDA Staff Training Form. The form is a training record, not a policy checklist.
5. **Share what the rules require.** Give each individual and proponent enough information about the grievance process to use it (COMAR 10.22.02.10D). Give families the executive summary of the emergency plan on request (COMAR 10.22.02.10B).
6. **Submit it when required.** The DDA Qualified Provider Application states that if DDA approves the application, the policies and procedures must be submitted to OHCQ within 30 days of approval. Confirm the current requirement with DDA.
7. **Keep it current.** Review the manual at least annually and whenever a regulation, the waiver, a DDA instruction, a PSP change, an incident trend, a survey finding or a plan of correction calls for a change. The official checklist asks whether each policy was modified since the last OHCQ survey, so keep a revision log that shows what changed and when. Re-adopt significant changes through the governing body and retrain staff on them.

**Adoption and revision record**

| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| Manual adopted by governing body on | [DATE] |
| Signed by (Board Chair) | [NAME / SIGNATURE] |
| Administrative head | [NAME] |
| Last full review | [DATE] |
| Next scheduled review | [DATE] |

**Note on source text.** Some rule summaries used to prepare this manual were taken from DDA research and not re-checked against the current online text. Before adoption, confirm each cited rule against the current version on the sources linked below.

## Regulatory Framework

### Governing rules

This manual is built on the following authorities. Cites are given exactly as they appear in the rules and source documents.

**Maryland licensing regulations (COMAR Title 10, Subtitle 22)**

- **COMAR 10.22.02** – Chapter 02, Administrative Requirements for Licensees (.01-1 through .14). Authority: Health-General §§7-904 and 7-909.
- **COMAR 10.22.02.01-1** – License Required. A license is required to provide community residential services.
- **COMAR 10.22.02.02** – Application for Initial License or Renewal. Covers corporate status, governing body responsibility, application contents, renewal filing at least 60 days before expiration, voluntary surrender, and termination of services to an individual only for good cause with the Director's written approval and notice of the right to a hearing under COMAR 10.22.16.
- **COMAR 10.22.02.03** – Investigation by the Administration. Sets OHCQ investigation priorities. Priority 1 (immediate jeopardy) investigations start within 2 working days.
- **COMAR 10.22.02.04** – Compliance Monitoring. Covers OHCQ surveys and visits, and plans of correction (POC) due at the exit conference or within 10 working days of receiving the findings. The POC deadline is in .04E, not .03.
- **COMAR 10.22.02.05** – New Site, Site Closure, or Relocation. DDA approval is required at least 30 days in advance.
- **COMAR 10.22.02.06** – Licensed Capacity.
- **COMAR 10.22.02.08** – Governing Body.
- **COMAR 10.22.02.09** – Program Service Plan (PSP).
- **COMAR 10.22.02.10** – Policies and Procedures. This is the regulation behind the official policy checklist.
- **COMAR 10.22.02.11** – Staffing Requirements, including training under .11C and .11D.
- **COMAR 10.22.02.12** – Health and Safety Requirements.
- **COMAR 10.22.02.13** – Records.
- **COMAR 10.22.02.14** – Quality Assurance.
- **COMAR 10.22.08.03** – Scope (Community Residential Services).
- **COMAR 10.22.08.04** – Staffing and Training (Community Residential Services).

**Waiver, Medicaid and federal requirements**

- **Community Pathways Waiver, Appendix C — Community Living – Group Home** (service definition, residence requirements, provider standards).
- **Community Pathways Waiver, Appendix I** (financial accountability).
- **42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)** (HCBS settings requirements).
- **42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)** (additional requirements for provider-owned or controlled residential settings).
- **29 CFR 1910.1030** (OSHA bloodborne pathogens), incorporated by reference in COMAR 10.22.02.11C(3).
- **DDA Addendum for Participation in Maryland Medical Assistance Program — PT 90 DDA** (separate MA number per licensed site).
- **Provider Portal Residential Services 2023 Billing Update (Jan 27, 2023)** (Number of People Authorized and retainer days).
- **DDA Addendum for Licensed Services and Sites (MDH Form DD.ADD.1.0, 06.02.2022)** (site addendum with Community Settings Rule attestation).
- **DDA New Site Visit Checklist (Community Settings Rule), Nov 14, 2022** (new site inspection form).
- **Staff Training Form DD.APP.1.1 (COMAR 10.22.02.11C&D)** (documents the .11C and .11D training topics).

**Employment law that applies to staff**

- **Md. Code, Labor & Employment §3-1304** (earned sick and safe leave).
- **Maryland Wage and Hour Law facts (MD Labor)** (state and local minimum wage).

Other statutes and regulations cited inside COMAR 10.22.02.10 and .11 apply as written. They include Health-General §7-1002, §7-1010 and §5-605, COMAR 10.27.11, Health-General §19-1902 et seq., and COMAR 12.15.03. Maryland rates and minimum wages change, so confirm current figures before relying on them.

### Regulators and contacts

| Regulator | Role | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **Maryland Department of Health — Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA)** | Approves qualified providers and licensed sites, operates the Community Pathways Waiver, authorizes services and dedicated hours, and sets LTSSMaryland rates. The DDA Director issues and denies licenses. | Web: https://health.maryland.gov/dda/Pages/Providers.aspx · Email: providerapplications.dda@maryland.gov |
| **MDH Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ) — Developmental Disabilities Team** | Licensing and monitoring agent for DDA. Conducts licensure and new-site surveys and complaint and incident investigations. | Web: https://health.maryland.gov/ohcq/Pages/Developmental-Disabilities.aspx · Phone: 410-402-8100 / 877-402-8220 |
| **Maryland Medicaid — Office of Medicaid Provider Services (MPRIME)** | Medicaid enrollment (MA number per licensed site, PT 90 DDA), revalidation and SDAT good-standing checks. | Web: https://www.mprime.health.maryland.gov · Phone: 1-844-463-7768 · Email: mdh.mprimegolive@maryland.gov |
| **Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)** | Approves the 1915(c) Community Pathways Waiver and its amendments. Enforces the HCBS settings rule. | Web: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-C/part-441/subpart-G/section-441.301 (no phone or email on file) |

Add [AGENCY NAME]'s assigned DDA regional office and OHCQ contacts to the customized manual.

### Official policy checklist and application documents

[AGENCY NAME]'s manual is reviewed against these documents:

1. **DH Form DD.APP.1.1 – Policies and Procedures (COMAR 10.22.02.10), version 02/18** (Maryland Department of Health / DDA). This is the checklist the reviewer uses. For each policy item the provider marks **Present: Yes, No or N/A**, and marks whether the policy was **modified since the last OHCQ survey**. The provider attaches its policies and procedures document. Every item marked "No" needs an explanation and a compliance plan in the box at the end of the form. DDA's website copy is also marked 02/18, and no newer version was found. Confirm the current version with DDA before submitting.
   Form: https://health.maryland.gov/dda/Documents/Policies%20and%20Procedures%20DH%20Form%20DD.APP.1.1.pdf
2. **COMAR 10.22.02.10 – Policies and Procedures.** This is the regulation text behind the form. It supplies the sub-items (a)–(g), (a)–(c) and (a)–(b) that the form's B(1), B(3) and B(5) refer to without spelling out.
   Text: https://regs.maryland.gov/us/md/exec/comar/10.22.02.10

Two related DDA documents are not policy checklists:
- **Staff Training Form DD.APP.1.1 (COMAR 10.22.02.11C&D)** is a training-record form, not a policy list. Staff training is addressed in this manual under the staffing and training policies and is documented on that form.
- The **DDA Qualified Provider Application** states that, if DDA approves the application, the policies and procedures must be submitted to OHCQ within 30 days of approval.

### Appendix A: how the official items are mapped

**Appendix A maps every official checklist item to the policy that satisfies it.** The items follow the form's own numbering and wording: A(1)–A(19), B(1)–B(7), C, D, and Nursing-1 to Nursing-7. For each item, Appendix A gives the item ID, the official wording, the policy section and page in this manual, and a space to record the Present Yes/No/N/A answer and whether the policy was modified since the last OHCQ survey. Note that the form's wording for A(8) and A(9) is shorter than the regulation's. A(8) says "MATP" on the form, while the regulation refers to the Administration's curriculum on medication training. The manual's policy language follows the regulation.

### Adoption, currency and training obligations

- **Customize.** The manual is a template. [AGENCY NAME] and all other placeholders must be replaced, and policies must describe the agency's real practices.
- **Adopt.** The governing body must formally adopt the manual and any significant revisions. It is legally responsible for oversight and compliance (COMAR 10.22.02.02A(2)–(3) and COMAR 10.22.02.08).
- **Keep current.** Update the manual when rules, DDA instructions, the PSP or QA plan, or survey findings change. Keep a revision log, since the official checklist asks whether each policy changed since the last OHCQ survey. Submit a revised PSP for DDA approval before implementing changes (COMAR 10.22.02.09B).
- **Train staff.** All staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers must know and implement every policy (COMAR 10.22.02.10C). Required job-specific and DDA-approved training must be completed before independent duties or within the timelines in COMAR 10.22.02.11C and D, and documented.

citations.requirement: A.(1): the licensee must be a Maryland corporation, or a foreign corporation registered in MD. A.(2)-(3): the governing body is legally responsible for overseeing all programs and for compliance. A.(4): the application needs a business plan, a DD experience summary, prior licensing reports from the last 10 years, and a DDA-approved QA plan. B.: file renewal at least 60 days before the license expires. D.: the Director may approve, approve with conditions, deny, or request more information. F.: voluntary surrender needs a closure schedule submitted at least 90 days ahead and approved by the Director. G.: terminate services to an individual only for good cause with the Director's written approval. Give the Director 90 days' written notice, give the individual and proponent written notice of the right to a hearing under COMAR 10.22.16, and copy the regional office and team. Services are considered terminated after 60 consecutive days' absence unless the Director decides otherwise.

citations.title: Investigation by the Administration
citations.requirement: Sets OHCQ investigation priorities. Priority 1 (immediate jeopardy) investigations start within 2 working days. Taken from the fact-checked research. NOTE: the fetched text of .04E, not .03, contains the 10-working-day plan-of-correction rule; cite .04E for the POC deadline.

citations.title: Compliance Monitoring
citations.requirement: A.: OHCQ, as the Administration's agent, monitors and inspects licensees. B.: an on-site pre-licensure survey is required. C.: announced and unannounced licensure visits happen at least annually. D.: announced or unannounced complaint investigation visits. E.: submit a plan of correction (POC) at the exit conference or within 10 working days of receiving the findings. OHCQ may require it sooner, and the OHCQ Director may grant an extension of up to 30 days. F.: if a POC is unacceptable, resubmit a revised POC within 10 working days.

citations.title: New Site, Site Closure, or Relocation
citations.requirement: DDA approval is required at least 30 days in advance to open, close or relocate a site. Taken from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Licensed Capacity
citations.requirement: The license states the number of people that may be served. Exceeding it requires Director approval, for a maximum of 60 days plus one 60-day extension. Taken from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Governing Body
citations.requirement: Board membership must include at least 1 person with a DD, 1 family member of a person with a DD, and 1 person with DD experience. At least 75% of members must live in MD or within 100 miles. No employees or their immediate family may be voting members. Bylaws must cover oversight, compliance, mission/budget/policy approval, conflict of interest, POC responses and PSP approval. Board members and employees may not own property leased back to the licensee (.08C(9)). Taken from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Program Service Plan (PSP)
citations.requirement: A.: a PSP is required for each service the licensee provides. B.: submit a revised PSP for DDA approval before implementing changes. C.: the administrative head ensures the governing body reviews and updates the PSP at least every 3 years. D.: comply with the approved PSP. E.: contents are rationale, scope, staffing and training, and setting and location (including the number of individuals expected to be served).

citations.title: Policies and Procedures
citations.requirement: A.(1)-(19) requires written policies on: health and safety per the IP; fundamental rights (Health-General §7-1002); promoting choice; confidentiality (Health-General §7-1010); a grievance process with anti-retaliation safeguards; nondiscrimination; reporting and investigating all incidents under DDA procedures; medication administration per DDA's curriculum; compliance with COMAR 10.27.11; behavior safeguards; property-damage payment; Health-General §5-605; no conflict of interest; GAAP fiscal practices; protection of individuals' finances (A(15)(a)-(e)); infection control and standard precautions; a disaster and evacuation plan with sufficient drills; and no individual performing paid staff duties or non-household tasks (A(18)-(19)). B.: group homes need an emergency plan covering evacuation or 72-hour shelter-in-place, an annual practice drill coordinated with local emergency planners, an after-action report and improvement plan, ID with health information, family and DDA regional office notification, staff recall, continuity of operations, off-site data backup, sharing the plan with local emergency management, and an executive summary for families on request. C.: all staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers must know and implement every policy. D.: give each individual and proponent enough information about the grievance process to use it.

citations.title: Staffing Requirements
citations.requirement: A.: analyze the number of individuals and each person's needs, then develop and implement a staffing plan that meets health and safety needs and delivers the IP services. There is no fixed numeric ratio. B.: no employing or contracting with anyone whose criminal history indicates behavior potentially harmful to individuals (Health-General §19-1902 et seq.; COMAR 12.15.03). C.: before independent duties, staff need job training, DDA-approved training (seizure disorders, principles of behavior change, management of disruptive behaviors, medication administration, aging) and OSHA blood-borne pathogens training under 29 CFR 1910.1030. D.: within 3 months of hire, DDA-approved training on community integration, individual-directed planning, characteristics and needs, First Aid/CPR (American Red Cross or equivalent), fundamental rights, communicable diseases, supporting choice, and communication skills. E.: written job descriptions and a policy to prevent employment discrimination.

citations.title: Health and Safety Requirements
citations.requirement: A.: each home must meet local zoning (except as provided in Health-General §7-603), local and State building codes and life-safety requirements, be free of hazards, and be in good repair. B.: free of fire hazards, with adequate smoke detectors, working and updated fire extinguishers, and a written fire evacuation plan. C.: water temperature at a maximum of 110°F unless every resident can regulate it safely and this is documented in each IP. D.: administer medication per DDA's medication curriculum, use unit-dose packaging for oral solids unless the IP says otherwise, package medication for absent individuals separately, and request pharmacy-generated MARs, TARs and physician order forms.

citations.title: Records
citations.requirement: A.: keep each individual's records at the site where the person is served. B.: minimum contents are application identifying information, emergency contact, next of kin, physician, diagnosis, allergies, medication list, the IP (COMAR 10.22.05), documentation of IP implementation, and anything else DDA requires. C.: on a medical emergency, make the person's medical information readily accessible to emergency personnel. D.: keep records at least 6 years, even if the person leaves or dies. Keep current-service documents for as long as the person is served, and organize records for easy access. E.: electronic records must meet the chapter, comply with HIPAA privacy and security rules, and be backed up and stored off-site.

citations.title: Quality Assurance
citations.requirement: A.: submit the QA plan and any substantive changes to DDA for approval. B.: an internal QA system that is focused on individual choice, preference and satisfaction (with personal contact), has measurable outcomes, analyzes trends, responds promptly when health or safety is at risk, and tracks behavior-plan restrictive techniques (who, which technique, date/time, emergency vs. plan, effectiveness). C.: set goals and standards, keep records, and implement changes based on the data. E.: standing committee(s) must review the incident protocol and all incidents, approve all behavior plans that use restrictive techniques, review and set time frames for rights restrictions not related to challenging behavior, and review policies for protection of rights. The committee must have equal numbers of licensee staff and non-employees (individuals, proponents or community members). Members may not decide on incidents or behavior plans they were involved in. It meets as needed with a majority present and must ensure confidentiality under Health-General §7-1010.

policies.title: Health and Safety Needs Met per the Individual Plan; Implementation of Supports and Daily Documentation
policies.applies_to: All staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers of [AGENCY NAME] who support individuals in the group home
policies.purpose: To make sure that each individual's health and safety needs, as identified in the Individual Plan (IP), are met every day and that the supports delivered are documented in the individual's record.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] meets each individual's health and safety needs as identified in the IP. This policy meets COMAR 10.22.02.10A(1) and DH Form DD.APP.1.1 p.1, item A(1) — Each individual's health and safety needs, as identified in the IP, are being met. Staffing levels and patterns are those determined in the IP (COMAR 10.22.08.04A). Services are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with back-up and emergency support, as the Community Pathways Waiver requires for Community Living – Group Home. Staff deliver the supports in each person's IP, and document implementation daily in the individual's record kept at the site where the person is served (COMAR 10.22.02.13B). Staff do not change, skip or substitute an IP support on their own. Questions or needed changes go to the Program Director and the IP team.

definitions.definition: The person-centered plan developed under COMAR 10.22.05 that identifies the person's goals, services, supports, and health and safety needs.
Any support, monitoring, equipment, diet, medication, supervision level or precaution identified in the IP or by a clinician that is required to keep the person healthy and safe.
A dated, signed (or electronically authenticated) record of the supports delivered, the person's response, and any change or concern, kept in the individual's record.
The person designated by [AGENCY NAME] as responsible for day-to-day operation of the home: [ADMINISTRATOR NAME].

procedures: Before a new individual moves in, the Program Director obtains the current IP and any addenda, assessments, health care orders, behavior plan, risk plans and dietary orders, and files them in the individual's record at the site.

The Program Director or designee extracts each health and safety need from the IP into a one-page Support Summary (supervision level, health conditions, allergies, diet, mobility, seizure and choking protocols, medications, behavior supports, communication method) and places it where on-duty staff can use it, consistent with privacy.

Before working independently with an individual, each staff member reads the IP sections and Support Summary that apply to that person. The staff member signs and dates a read-and-understood acknowledgment, which is filed in the personnel record.

The Program Director sets the staffing schedule so that staffing levels and patterns match those determined in the IP for each individual (COMAR 10.22.08.04A). Any shift that cannot be filled to the required level is escalated immediately to the Program Director or on-call administrator (see SP-01 and EP-04).
The home maintains 24/7 service availability. The on-call administrator’s name and [PHONE] number are posted for staff on every shift and updated whenever the on-call schedule changes.

On each shift, staff deliver the supports assigned to that shift in the IP and Support Summary, including health monitoring, diet and fluid instructions, positioning, mobility aids, supervision and community activities.

On each shift, staff record on the daily support log what was provided, when, the individual's response or participation, and any refusal, change in condition, injury or concern. Entries are made at or near the time of service, never in advance, and each entry is signed or initialed with the staff member's full name identified.

Staff immediately report a change in health condition, a missed support, or a safety concern to the shift lead and the Program Director, and follow HW-02 for medical emergencies and PA-06 for reportable incidents.

Staff do not alter documentation after the fact. A correction is made by drawing a single line through the error, writing the correct information, and dating and initialing it. Electronic records use an audit-trail correction.

The Program Director reviews daily support logs at least weekly. He or she checks that every IP support was delivered and documented, follows up with staff on gaps the same day, and records the review with a signature and date.
The RN Health Care Coordinator or delegating nurse reviews health-related documentation as described in NU-07 and reports health and safety gaps to the Program Director.

The Program Director meets with the individual, proponent, and IP team as required by the IP process in COMAR 10.22.05 to review whether supports are meeting health and safety needs. Needed changes are requested through the DDA coordinator of community services, and are put into practice only after the IP is updated.

When the IP is revised, the Program Director updates the Support Summary within one working day of receiving the revised IP, retrains staff on the changes before the next shift on which they work, and files new acknowledgments.

Unmet needs, repeated documentation gaps and support-delivery failures are logged and reported to the Quality Assurance process (GOV-03). Where a gap rises to a reportable incident (for example, neglect), it is handled under PA-06 and BP-01.
Daily logs, Support Summaries and acknowledgments are retained in the individual's record per REC-01 (at least 6 years, even if the person leaves or dies) (COMAR 10.22.02.13D).

Obtains and files IPs, builds Support Summaries, schedules staff to IP-determined levels, reviews documentation weekly, and corrects gaps.
Reviews health-related supports and documentation, and advises the Program Director on health needs.
Read the IP, deliver each support, document daily, and report changes and concerns immediately.
Participate in IP meetings and tell [AGENCY NAME] when supports are not meeting the person's needs.

Support Summary for each individual
Staff read-and-understood acknowledgments
Daily support logs documenting IP implementation
Weekly Program Director log review sheets
Staffing schedules showing IP-determined levels and patterns
