Staff must not charge residents for transportation, and must not accept money or gifts for providing rides (see PA-12, SP-05). If a resident chooses to use a personal vehicle, a ride from a family member or a paid transit option, the choice is documented.

Staff may drive their own vehicles to transport residents only with advance written approval from the Program Director, and only after proof of license, registration and insurance is verified and filed.
The Program Director reviews vehicle records, driver files, accidents and rider feedback each quarter in the quality assurance review (see GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Hold a valid license and current First Aid/CPR, check the vehicle, secure riders, drive safely and report any incident or license change.
Schedule cost-effective, safe transportation, verify licenses and insurance, ensure vehicle maintenance and respond to incidents.
Document transportation needs and preferences and promote travel skills and independence.
Maintain insurance coverage and fund vehicle maintenance and accessible transportation.
Use seat belts and securement, and share their transportation preferences.

documentation: Transportation needs and preferences in the IP
Driver's license copies, driving record checks and First Aid/CPR certificates in personnel files
Vehicle registration, insurance and inspection records
Vehicle maintenance and pre-trip check logs
Accident and incident reports
Vehicle evacuation drill records
Written approval for any staff use of a personal vehicle

policies.title: Staffing Plan, Supervision and Awake Overnight Staff
policies.applies_to: [AGENCY NAME] administrators, supervisors and all direct support staff at every licensed Community Living – Group Home site
policies.purpose: To ensure each home has enough qualified staff, scheduled in the right patterns, to meet each person's health and safety needs and to deliver the services in the Individual Plan (IP) at all times, including overnight and in emergencies.
policies.policy: Maryland sets no fixed staff-to-resident ratio. Instead, [AGENCY NAME] analyzes the number of individuals in each home and each person's needs, then develops and implements a written staffing plan that meets health and safety needs and delivers the services in each IP (COMAR 10.22.02.11A). Staffing levels and patterns follow what is determined in the IP (COMAR 10.22.08.04A). Services are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week at each licensed site, with back-up and emergency support (Community Pathways Waiver, Appendix C – Community Living – Group Home). Where an individual's IP calls for overnight supervision, [AGENCY NAME] provides awake overnight staff. The DDA rate for a four-person home with overnight supervision funds 43.14 staff-hours per day. That figure is a rate assumption used for budgeting and is not a regulatory ratio, and actual staffing is set by the needs analysis and IPs. [AGENCY NAME] does not reduce staffing below what the IP and the staffing plan require because of cost or vacancy. No relative, legal guardian or legally responsible person of a resident may be paid to provide this service. Staff are at least 18 years old, hold First Aid/CPR and have completed an in-person skills check (Community Pathways Waiver, Appendix C). Training is provided or arranged under COMAR 10.22.02.11 and 10.22.08.04B (see SP-03). All staff must know and implement this policy (COMAR 10.22.02.10C).

definitions.definition: A written plan for each home showing the needs analysis, the number and types of staff by shift, supervision levels, back-up and emergency coverage, and how the IP services will be delivered.
A staff member who is awake, alert and on duty in the home for the entire overnight period, and is not permitted to sleep.
The number of staff and the days and hours they work, as determined by the IP and the staffing plan.
Additional one-to-one or extra staff hours authorized by DDA for a person whose needs exceed the basic residential service.
A person with a legal duty to support the individual, such as a spouse or the parent of a minor, who may not be paid for this service.

procedures: Before a home opens and at least annually, the Program Director analyzes the number of residents and each person's needs, using the IP, health and behavior information, communication needs, mobility, medical needs, medication needs, community activities, work and day schedules, and risk assessments.

The Program Director writes the staffing plan for each home. It states the number and type of staff for each shift on weekdays, weekends and holidays, supervision levels (including overnight and during community outings), and the rationale tied to the needs analysis.

The plan identifies the times when residents are home, the times when they are out, and the support needed for medical appointments, outings and employment, so that staffing covers both. Dedicated hours authorized by DDA are scheduled and tracked separately.

The Program Director confirms that staffing in the plan meets or exceeds what each IP calls for. If the plan is lower than any IP requires, the plan is revised before it is used. A staffing level is never set simply from the funded rate.

The Program Director schedules awake overnight staff for each night in any home where an IP requires overnight supervision, and does so in every home unless the staffing analysis and IPs show a different arrangement is safe, the team agrees, and the decision is documented. Awake overnight staff are not permitted to sleep and stay in the home for the full shift.

Each schedule is posted at least two weeks ahead, and shows each person scheduled, the shift and the supervisor or on-call administrator. The schedule is kept with actual hours worked, with time records, to show that staffing delivered matched the plan.

At all times at least one qualified staff member is in the home when a resident who needs supervision is present. No one is left unsupervised against their IP. Staff do not leave their post until relieved, and handoff is documented.

Every staff member assigned to a home meets the qualifications of SP-02, SP-03 and SP-04. This includes being at least 18, having First Aid/CPR and an in-person skills check, and completing required training before independent duties. Staff who give medication hold Medication Technician certification from the Board of Nursing, or are licensed nurses, and follow PA-07.
Staff are oriented to each person's IP and supports before working with the person. New staff work alongside experienced staff until their competence has been checked and documented.

The agency maintains back-up and emergency support at all times: an on-call administrator reachable by phone 24/7, a list of back-up staff, and a call-out procedure. The on-call number, [PHONE], is posted in every home. Back-up arrangements link to EP-04 for emergencies.

If a shift cannot be filled, the supervisor first calls back-up staff and the on-call administrator, who authorizes overtime, agency staff or administrative staff to cover. The shift is not left short. If minimum safe staffing cannot be met, the on-call administrator takes steps to keep residents safe, and notifies the Program Director and DDA as required.

The agency does not hire, contract with or pay relatives, legal guardians or legally responsible persons of a resident to provide this service. The Program Director checks relationships at hire and at each new admission, and removes the person from the schedule for that resident if a conflict arises (see PA-12).
Staff must not leave residents to be supervised by other residents, or assign residents to perform paid staff duties (see PA-16).

When a resident's needs change, the team reviews the staffing plan within a short time and revises it, including requests to DDA for added dedicated hours when authorized services are not enough. Staffing is not reduced for a vacancy without reviewing each remaining resident's needs.

The Program Director reviews the staffing plan at least quarterly and when any resident is admitted, discharged or has a change of condition, and compares planned with actual staffing, absences, overtime, incidents and complaints.
Findings are reported to the quality assurance committee (see GOV-03), and any gap between required and actual staffing is corrected immediately and documented.

responsibilities.duty: Work scheduled shifts, stay awake and alert on overnight shifts, supervise per the IP, complete handoffs and report staffing problems at once.
Analyze needs, write and update the staffing plan, make schedules, arrange coverage and ensure staff qualifications.
Be reachable 24/7, arrange back-up and emergency coverage, and make decisions when staff are short.
Ensure the agency funds the staffing the plan requires and that no one prohibited from being paid is employed for this service.
Identify each person's supervision and support needs in the IP and revisit them when needs change.

documentation: Written staffing plan for each home with needs analysis and rationale
Staff schedules and actual time records, including overnight
Back-up staff and on-call lists
Records of dedicated hours authorized and delivered
Staff qualification, certification and training records
Documentation of review of relationships to individuals (no payment to relatives, guardians or legally responsible persons)
Quarterly staffing review notes and corrective actions

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors, consultants, volunteers and board-assigned personnel who have direct contact with individuals at any [AGENCY NAME] Community Living – Group Home site
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] does not employ or contract with anyone whose criminal history or exclusion status indicates a risk of harm to the people we support.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not employ or contract with any person whose criminal history indicates behavior that is potentially harmful to individuals, as required by COMAR 10.22.02.11B. The background-check requirements cited there are Health-General §19-1902 et seq. and COMAR 12.15.03. Every person who will have direct contact with individuals must complete a background check, and the result must be cleared before the person starts work, begins a contract assignment or begins volunteering. This applies to employees, contractors, consultants and volunteers. [AGENCY NAME] also screens each person against the federal OIG exclusion list and the Maryland sanctioned provider list before hire or engagement and on an ongoing basis. Results are recorded on the Staff Criminal History form and kept in the personnel or contractor file. No one works alone with an individual until clearance is documented.

definitions.definition: Any in-person, unsupervised or regular contact with an individual, including providing support, transportation, health care, maintenance work in the home, or volunteering.

definitions.term: Criminal history indicating potentially harmful behavior
definitions.definition: A record of convictions, pending charges or findings that, in the judgment of the Administrator applying COMAR 12.15.03 and Health-General §19-1902 et seq., suggest a risk of harm to individuals.
The federal OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities and the Maryland sanctioned (excluded) provider list.
The form on which [AGENCY NAME] records each check, its date, its result and the clearance decision.

procedures: Before making any offer, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] or designee tells every applicant in writing that employment is conditional on a satisfactory criminal history check and registry/exclusion screening.
The applicant signs the consent and disclosure forms needed to run the checks. Missing or refused consent ends the hiring process.

The Administrator or designee starts the criminal history check required under COMAR 10.22.02.11B, COMAR 12.15.03 and Health-General §19-1902 et seq. before the person's first day of work, contract assignment or volunteer shift.

Before the start date, the designee screens the person against the federal OIG exclusion list and the Maryland sanctioned provider list. The designee prints or saves the result with the date, the name of the person who ran it and the search criteria.
The designee completes the Staff Criminal History form with the check date, the result and the clearance decision, and places it in the personnel file. The Administrator signs the decision.

If a record is returned, the Administrator reviews the offense, how long ago it occurred, its relationship to the duties and any available court or agency documents. The review is documented. The Administrator decides whether the history indicates behavior potentially harmful to individuals. If it does, the person is not hired, engaged or allowed to volunteer.
If the person appears on an exclusion list, they are not hired, engaged or allowed to volunteer, and the Administrator documents the decision.
No one may be scheduled alone with an individual, or counted in the staffing plan, until the Staff Criminal History form shows clearance.

Contractors and consultants with direct contact (for example nurses, therapists, maintenance staff and drivers) must be checked in the same way. Where a contracting firm runs its own checks, [AGENCY NAME] obtains written proof of clearance and keeps it on file, or runs its own check.
Volunteers are checked before their first contact with an individual and are never left unsupervised until cleared.

Every employee, contractor and volunteer must report to the Administrator within one business day any new arrest, charge, conviction or exclusion. Failure to report is grounds for discipline up to termination.

The designee re-screens all active staff and contractors against the OIG and Maryland lists at least monthly, and also at each annual evaluation. Each re-screen is documented. A positive result leads to immediate removal from direct contact pending Administrator review.

The Administrator reviews the personnel files at least quarterly to confirm every person with direct contact has a completed Staff Criminal History form and current exclusion screening. Gaps are corrected the same day.
Check results are confidential. They are kept in the personnel file, are not shared with other staff and are disclosed only to authorized regulators.

responsibilities.duty: Makes clearance decisions, signs the Staff Criminal History form, enforces the no-start-before-clearance rule, and reviews files quarterly.
Initiates the checks, runs the exclusion screenings, completes the forms and keeps them current.
Receives a summary of compliance during quality assurance reviews.
Cooperate with checks and promptly report any new charge, conviction or exclusion.

documentation: Signed consent and disclosure forms
Staff Criminal History form with Administrator's clearance decision
Dated printouts of OIG and Maryland sanctioned provider list screenings (initial and ongoing)
Written records of review of any criminal record returned

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Orientation and Training
policies.applies_to: All direct support professionals, supervisors, relief staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers who support individuals at [AGENCY NAME] sites
policies.purpose: To make sure every person who supports individuals is trained before working independently and completes the remaining required training within the time allowed, so that supports are safe and match each Individual Plan.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides or arranges training in accordance with COMAR 10.22.02.11 (COMAR 10.22.08.04B). Before performing independent duties, each staff member must complete (1) job training, (2) DDA-approved training in seizure disorders, principles of behavior change, management of disruptive behaviors, medication administration and aging, and (3) OSHA blood-borne pathogens training under 29 CFR 1910.1030 (COMAR 10.22.02.11C). Within 3 months of hire, each staff member must complete DDA-approved training in community integration, individual-directed planning, characteristics and needs of people served, First Aid/CPR (American Red Cross or equivalent), fundamental rights, communicable diseases, supporting choice, and communication skills (COMAR 10.22.02.11D). Staff are at least 18 years old and hold current First Aid/CPR with an in-person skills check. Unlicensed staff who give medication must hold a Medication Technician certification from the Maryland Board of Nursing and work under RN delegation (see PA-07 and NU-07). All training is recorded on Staff Training Form DD.APP.1.1. [AGENCY NAME] budgets about 27.3 training hours per full-time-equivalent employee per year, which is the figure DDA's rate assumes, and also provides ongoing training based on individuals' needs.

definitions.definition: Providing support to an individual without a trained, qualified staff member present. Shadowing and observation do not count as independent duties.
Training content, curriculum or trainers approved by the Developmental Disabilities Administration for the topics listed in COMAR 10.22.02.11C and D.
An unlicensed person certified by the Maryland Board of Nursing to administer medication under delegation.
The DDA form used to document the COMAR 10.22.02.11C and D training topics.

procedures: On hire, the Administrator or Training Coordinator opens a training record for the employee using Staff Training Form DD.APP.1.1 and sets a training calendar with the 3-month deadline from hire date.
The employee may begin orientation shifts only as a shadow, counted as additional staff beyond the staffing plan, until all pre-independent training is complete and signed off.

Job training: a trained senior staff member or supervisor orients the employee to the home, individuals' Individual Plans, daily routines, emergency procedures, and this Policy Manual. The trainer signs and dates what was covered.

The employee completes DDA-approved training in seizure disorders, principles of behavior change, management of disruptive behaviors, medication administration and aging before independent duties. Certificates or rosters are filed.
The employee completes OSHA blood-borne pathogens training under 29 CFR 1910.1030 before independent duties, and receives an annual refresher. The Training Coordinator records the date and trainer.

The Training Coordinator confirms every item in C above is documented on Form DD.APP.1.1 before the Administrator signs the 'Cleared for Independent Duties' line. The employee is then added to the staffing schedule as counted staff.

Individual-specific training: before working alone with an individual, the employee is trained by a supervisor or the RN on that individual's Individual Plan, health and safety needs, communication, behavior support plan (if any), diet and choking precautions, and seizure protocol (if any). Training is documented.

Within 3 months of hire, the employee completes DDA-approved training in community integration, individual-directed planning, characteristics and needs of people served, fundamental rights, communicable diseases, supporting choice, and communication skills.

Within the same 3 months, the employee completes First Aid/CPR from the American Red Cross or an equivalent provider, with an in-person skills check. Online-only courses do not count. The card is copied to the file, and renewal dates are tracked.

Staff who will give medication must hold a current Medication Technician certification from the Board of Nursing and must not pass medication until they are certified and delegated under NU-07. Others do not administer medication.

The Training Coordinator reviews all training records monthly, flags items due within 30 days, and notifies the Administrator of any overdue item. A staff member with overdue required training is removed from unsupervised duties until the training is completed.

Annual plan: [AGENCY NAME] plans for about 27.3 training hours per full-time-equivalent employee each year, including refreshers, changes in individuals' needs, rights, emergency drills and policy updates. The Administrator adjusts the plan based on incident trends and Quality Assurance findings.

Contractors, consultants and volunteers who have contact with individuals receive orientation proportionate to their role, including rights, abuse reporting and emergency procedures. Volunteers are never counted in the staffing plan.
The Administrator reports training compliance to the Governing Body at least quarterly and to the Quality Assurance Standing Committee as part of GOV-03.

Schedules training, maintains Form DD.APP.1.1 and certificates, runs monthly compliance reviews.
Provides health-related and delegated-task training, and supervises Medication Technicians (see NU-07).

policies.title: Personnel Records, Employee Health Screening and Wage and Leave Compliance
policies.applies_to: All employees and the administrative staff responsible for personnel files, payroll and scheduling at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To keep complete, organized personnel records, protect staff and individuals through health screening and exposure control, and make sure employees are paid and given leave as Maryland law requires.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written job description for every position and a written policy to prevent employment discrimination (COMAR 10.22.02.11E). Each employee's personnel file contains training records, background-check records and, for medication technicians, certification records. [AGENCY NAME] provides blood-borne pathogens training and exposure follow-up in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.1030 (COMAR 10.22.02.11C). No COMAR requirement for tuberculosis or other health screening was identified in the research for this manual. [AGENCY NAME] therefore sets its own health screening requirements by policy, and the Administrator confirms current expectations with the local health department. [AGENCY NAME] pays at least the Maryland minimum wage of $15.00 per hour and any higher county minimum that applies to the work location, and provides earned sick and safe leave under Md. Code, Labor & Employment §3-1304.

definitions.definition: The confidential file for each employee containing hiring, training, background-check, certification, health-screening, wage and evaluation records.
Leave accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours per year, that is paid when the employer has 15 or more employees.
The highest of the Maryland state minimum ($15.00/hr) and the county minimum where the employee works.

procedures: The Administrator maintains a written job description for every position (including direct support professional, supervisor, relief staff and Registered Nurse). Each states duties, qualifications, reporting line and required training. Each employee signs a copy at hire and when it changes.

[AGENCY NAME] maintains and distributes to all staff a written policy to prevent employment discrimination. The Administrator reviews it annually and applies it to recruitment, hiring, pay, discipline and termination.

Each employee's personnel file contains: application and resume; signed job description; verification of age (18 or older) and credentials; Staff Criminal History form and exclusion screenings (SP-02); Staff Training Form DD.APP.1.1 and certificates (SP-03); First Aid/CPR card; Medication Technician certification where applicable; health screening records; evaluations; and wage and leave records.

Personnel files are kept in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system. Only the Administrator and designated HR staff may access them. Health information is kept separate from the rest of the file.

Health screening: before the first day of work, the employee provides the health screening documentation required by [AGENCY NAME]'s policy. Because no COMAR requirement was verified, the Administrator confirms the requirements with the local health department and records the confirmation date and the person contacted. The agency policy is re-checked annually.
Employees who show signs of a communicable illness do not work with individuals until cleared under PA-15. The supervisor documents the absence and the return.

Blood-borne pathogens: employees receive training before independent duties and annually (SP-03). The Administrator ensures the employer duties of 29 CFR 1910.1030 are met, including an exposure control plan, protective equipment, hepatitis B vaccination offered at no cost, and post-exposure evaluation and follow-up. Employees report any exposure to the supervisor immediately.

Wages: before hire and every January 1 and July 1, the designee confirms the applicable minimum wage for each site's county. The state minimum is $15.00 per hour. Montgomery County is $18.00 (51 or more employees), $16.50 (11-50 employees, and certain nonprofit and Medicaid-funded home care providers) or $15.95 (10 or fewer employees). Howard County is $16.00. Prince George's County is $15.30 (as of July 1, 2026). Any employee paid below the applicable minimum is corrected in the next payroll, including back pay.
The designee keeps time and payroll records for every employee, including hours worked, rate, overtime and deductions. Employees review and sign their time records each pay period.

Earned sick and safe leave: the payroll system credits 1 hour of leave for every 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours per year, from the employee's first day. The Administrator confirms headcount each year. At 15 or more employees the leave is paid. Below 15, the Administrator confirms the requirements under Labor & Employment §3-1304 before setting leave terms.
Employees may use earned sick and safe leave for qualifying reasons under §3-1304, and the supervisor documents each use. [AGENCY NAME] does not retaliate against any employee for using leave.
Supervisors arrange coverage for leave so staffing plan levels (SP-01) are maintained.
The Administrator audits all personnel files at least semi-annually for completeness, using a checklist, and corrects any gaps within 10 days. The audit results are reported to the Governing Body.
Personnel records are kept per [AGENCY NAME]'s retention schedule and made available to DDA and OHCQ on request.

Maintains files, tracks wage rates and leave balances, runs payroll accurately.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, care providers, consultants, contractors, volunteers and Governing Body members of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To protect individuals from exploitation and conflicts of interest by setting clear professional boundaries and conduct expectations.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] has no conflict of interest involving staff, care providers or volunteers (COMAR 10.22.02.10 A(13)). Individuals do not perform paid staff duties or non-household tasks for the agency (COMAR 10.22.02.10 A(18)). Staff may not borrow money or property from, sell anything to, or take money or gifts from individuals. [AGENCY NAME] does not pay relatives, legal guardians or legally responsible persons for providing this service (Community Pathways Waiver, Appendix C). Board members and employees may not own property leased back to [AGENCY NAME] (COMAR 10.22.02.08C(9)). Any misconduct that falls within the Policy on Reportable Incidents and Investigations (PORII) is reported as an incident under PA-06 and BP-01. This policy supports PA-12 (Conflict of Interest) and PA-16 (Individuals Not Performing Paid Staff Duties).

definitions.definition: The limit that separates a staff member's professional role from personal, financial or social relationships with an individual.

A situation in which a personal, financial or family interest of a staff member, care provider, volunteer or board member could influence, or appear to influence, decisions about individuals or the agency.
Behavior that violates this policy or other agency policies, including abuse, neglect, exploitation, boundary violations and financial misuse.
DDA's Policy on Reportable Incidents and Investigations.

procedures: At hire and annually, each staff member, care provider, contractor and volunteer receives this policy, signs an acknowledgment, and completes a conflict-of-interest disclosure. The Administrator reviews each disclosure and documents any action required.
Staff must not borrow money or items from, lend money to, or enter into any business or sales arrangement with an individual. Staff must not sell goods or services to an individual.

Staff must not accept money, gifts, tips, bequests or other benefits from an individual or an individual's family, except items of nominal value that the Administrator has approved in writing. When a gift is offered, staff politely decline and tell the supervisor.
Staff must not use an individual's funds, property, accounts, cards or benefits for themselves. Any handling of an individual's money follows PA-14, with receipts and two-person verification.
Staff must not use their position to seek personal favors, to direct an individual's choices of providers or services for personal gain, or to influence guardians or family members.

Individuals do not perform paid staff duties or non-household tasks for [AGENCY NAME]. Individuals may take part in ordinary household chores only as an individual choice and as stated in the Individual Plan (PA-16). Supervisors do not assign agency work to individuals.

Relatives, legal guardians and legally responsible persons of an individual are not hired or paid for providing this service to that individual. The Administrator checks relationships at hire and when an individual is admitted.

Board members and employees, and their immediate family, may not own property leased back to [AGENCY NAME] (COMAR 10.22.02.08C(9)). The Administrator checks leases and vendor relationships annually against the disclosures.

Staff keep relationships with individuals professional: no romantic or sexual relationships, no private social media connections, no sharing personal problems, no off-duty visits or private outings, and no taking individuals to staff's own homes, unless the Administrator has approved it in writing as an exception that is consistent with the individual's plan and rights.
Staff protect confidentiality at all times (PA-03) and do not photograph or post about individuals without documented consent.

Staff report suspected boundary violations, conflicts of interest or misconduct by anyone to the supervisor or Administrator immediately. If the Administrator is involved, the report goes to the Governing Body chair. Reporting follows BP-01 and PA-06. Retaliation against anyone who reports is prohibited.

When misconduct appears to be a reportable incident, the Administrator reports it under PORII (PA-06) within the required time, removes staff from contact with individuals as needed, and cooperates with OHCQ and law enforcement.
Substantiated violations lead to discipline up to termination. The Administrator documents the finding and the action in the personnel file.
The Administrator reviews disclosures and boundary issues annually with the Governing Body and the Quality Assurance Standing Committee (GOV-03).

Reviews conflict-of-interest disclosures for the Administrator and board members and oversees compliance.
Model boundaries, monitor practice and report concerns.

policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All staff who create, use, store or have access to individual records at [AGENCY NAME] sites
policies.purpose: To make sure each individual's record is complete, accessible when needed, protected under HIPAA, and kept for the required period.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps each individual's records at the site where the person is served (COMAR 10.22.02.13A). Each record contains at least: application and identifying information, emergency contact, next of kin, physician, diagnosis, allergies, medication list, the Individual Plan (COMAR 10.22.05), documentation of Individual Plan implementation, and anything else DDA requires (COMAR 10.22.02.13B). In a medical emergency, the individual's medical information is made readily accessible to emergency personnel (COMAR 10.22.02.13C). Records are kept at least 6 years, even if the individual leaves or dies. Documents about current services are kept for as long as the person is served, and records are organized for easy access (COMAR 10.22.02.13D). Electronic records meet COMAR 10.22.02, comply with the HIPAA privacy and security rules (45 CFR 164), and are backed up and stored off-site (COMAR 10.22.02.13E).

definitions.definition: The paper or electronic file for one individual containing the required contents and documentation of services.

A one-to-two page summary containing identifying information, diagnoses, allergies, medication list, physician, emergency contact and next of kin, kept where staff and emergency personnel can reach it immediately.
At least 6 years from the end of services, discharge or death.

procedures: At admission, the Program Director or designee opens an individual record at the site where the person lives and completes the identifying information (application, name, date of birth, guardian or representative, payer information).

Within the admission process, staff add: emergency contact, next of kin, physician, diagnosis, allergies, and the current medication list. The RN verifies the medication list against prescriber orders (NU-01).

The current Individual Plan (COMAR 10.22.05) is placed in the record as soon as it is finalized, and each update replaces the older version in the active section. Older versions are filed in an archive section.

Direct support staff record daily documentation of Individual Plan implementation (PA-01) at the time the support is given, with the date, time and staff signature or initials. Entries are never backdated.
Staff also file other items DDA requires, including consents, restrictions documentation, behavior plans, incident reports, health care coordination notes and releases.
The record is organized with labeled sections and an index so that any item can be found promptly by authorized staff and regulators.

Emergency access: an emergency information packet for each individual is kept in a known location in the home and in the go-bag used for evacuation and transport (EP-01). Staff send it with the individual to any ER or hospital and take it with them on any outing.
The Program Director reviews each paper record monthly for completeness and accuracy. Missing items are completed within 5 business days.

Access: only staff who need the information to provide services, the RN, the Administrator and authorized regulators may view records. Staff sign confidentiality agreements. Paper records are in locked cabinets, and electronic records require unique user IDs and passwords (PA-03).

Electronic records: [AGENCY NAME] uses systems that meet COMAR 10.22.02 and the HIPAA privacy and security rules (45 CFR 164), including access controls, audit logs, encryption where reasonably possible, and workforce HIPAA training.

Electronic records are backed up at least daily, and the backup is stored off-site or in a secure cloud service under a signed business associate agreement. The Administrator tests restoration at least quarterly and documents the test (EP-05).
Release of information is done only with valid written authorization or as the law allows. Staff log each release, and the Administrator reviews the log monthly.

Retention: records are kept at least 6 years from the end of services, discharge or death. Records of current services stay in the active record while the person is served. Closed records are boxed and labeled with the destroy-after date and stored securely.
Transfer or discharge: for a transfer, copies of the necessary records go to the receiving provider with authorization, and [AGENCY NAME] keeps the originals for the full retention period (PCS-04).
Destruction occurs only after the retention period ends and with the Administrator's written approval. Paper is shredded and electronic media is securely wiped. A destruction log is kept.
If a record is lost, damaged or accessed improperly, staff report it to the Administrator immediately. The Administrator follows PA-03 and PA-06 for breach and incident reporting.

Opens and maintains records at each site, reviews them monthly, ensures the emergency information packets are current.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State, Inspections and Plans of Correction
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Program Directors and all staff who interact with OHCQ, DDA or other regulators at [AGENCY NAME] sites
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] cooperates with state inspections and investigations, submits acceptable plans of correction on time, and makes the required reports and requests to DDA and OHCQ.
policies.policy: The Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), acting as the Administration's agent, monitors and inspects [AGENCY NAME] (COMAR 10.22.02.04A). OHCQ conducts an on-site pre-licensure survey (.04B), announced and unannounced licensure visits at least annually (.04C), and announced or unannounced complaint investigation visits (.04D). [AGENCY NAME] gives surveyors prompt access to the site, staff, individuals and records. [AGENCY NAME] submits a plan of correction (POC) at the exit conference or within 10 working days of receiving the findings. OHCQ may require it sooner, and the OHCQ Director may grant an extension of up to 30 days (COMAR 10.22.02.04E). If a POC is unacceptable, [AGENCY NAME] resubmits a revised POC within 10 working days (COMAR 10.22.02.04F). OHCQ investigations of immediate-jeopardy (Priority 1) matters begin within 2 working days (COMAR 10.22.02.03). [AGENCY NAME] reports incidents under DDA's PORII (see PA-06), seeks DDA approval at least 30 days ahead to open, close or relocate a site (COMAR 10.22.02.05), and stays within licensed capacity, seeking Director approval for any temporary overage (COMAR 10.22.02.06).

definitions.definition: A written plan responding to each finding of noncompliance, stating the corrective action, the person responsible and the date of completion.
The meeting at the end of an OHCQ survey at which findings are shared.
A situation OHCQ categorizes as an immediate jeopardy to individuals' health or safety, with investigation beginning within 2 working days.
The number of people the license states may be served at the site.
Monday through Friday, excluding State holidays.

procedures: Inspections: the Administrator and every Program Director know that OHCQ may arrive announced or unannounced at any time. Each site keeps a surveyor-ready folder with the license, current staffing schedule, emergency plan, drill records and the contact list.

When a surveyor arrives, the staff member in charge verifies identification, notifies the Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME], [PHONE]) immediately, and offers the surveyor access to the home, staff, individuals and records. Staff do not delay, hide or alter any record.
The Administrator or designee accompanies the surveyor, takes notes, tracks documents given and ensures that individuals' privacy and routines are respected.
The Administrator attends the exit conference when possible, listens to the findings and asks for clarification. The Administrator records findings and the dates received.

Within 1 working day of receiving written findings, the Administrator logs the date of receipt, calculates the due date (exit conference or 10 working days from receipt, or any earlier date OHCQ requires) and assigns a lead for each finding.

The POC states, for each finding, what will be corrected, how it will be done, who is responsible, the completion date, and how [AGENCY NAME] will monitor to prevent recurrence. Where practical, the POC addresses every individual who could be affected.

The Administrator reviews the POC with the Governing Body or its designee, consistent with the Governing Body's responsibility for responding to plans of correction (GOV-01), and submits it to OHCQ by the deadline. A dated copy of the submission and proof of delivery are kept.

If more time is needed, the Administrator asks the OHCQ Director in writing before the due date for an extension of up to 30 days (COMAR 10.22.02.04E). An extension is not assumed until it is granted in writing.
If OHCQ finds the POC unacceptable, the Administrator revises it and resubmits it within 10 working days (COMAR 10.22.02.04F), and the Governing Body is informed.

After acceptance, the lead for each finding completes the corrective action by the stated date and keeps evidence (training rosters, revised policies, photos, audits). The Quality Assurance Standing Committee verifies completion and checks for recurrence (GOV-03). Items from other required corrections are tracked using XP-01.

Complaint visits: when OHCQ notifies [AGENCY NAME] of a complaint, the Administrator cooperates fully, preserves all relevant records, protects the complainant from retaliation (PA-04) and treats immediate-jeopardy matters (Priority 1) as urgent, since OHCQ starts those within 2 working days.

Incident reports: the Administrator ensures that every reportable incident is reported to DDA and OHCQ under PORII within the required timeframe, and that investigations are carried out (PA-06). OHCQ may be reached at 410-402-8100 or 877-402-8220.

New site, closure or relocation: the Administrator submits a request to DDA at least 30 days before opening, closing or relocating a site (COMAR 10.22.02.05) and does not open, close or move until approval is received in writing. Individuals and their representatives are notified and transition planning follows PCS-04.

Capacity: the Administrator verifies before each admission that the number of people served will not exceed the licensed capacity (GOV-02). If exceeding capacity becomes necessary, the Administrator requests Director approval before the overage begins. Approval is for a maximum of 60 days, with one 60-day extension available (COMAR 10.22.02.06). The Administrator tracks the end date and documents the approval.

The Administrator keeps a regulatory log of all inspections, findings, POC submissions, extensions, incident reports and DDA approvals, and reports to the Governing Body at least quarterly. Records of surveys and POCs are kept in the administrative files for at least 6 years.

documents.how_used: This is the checklist the reviewer uses. For each policy item the provider marks Present Yes, No or N/A, and marks whether the policy was modified since the last OHCQ survey. The provider attaches its policies and procedures document. The provider must explain every item marked 'No' and give a plan to bring the agency into compliance. The item list below follows the form's own numbering and wording.

official.notes: The reviewer works from the two-page DH Form DD.APP.1.1 (02/18) checklist. The provider submits it together with a written policies and procedures document. For each item, the provider marks Present Yes, No or N/A, and marks whether the policy was modified since the last OHCQ survey. Every item marked 'No' needs an explanation and a compliance plan in the box at the end of the form. The safest way to organize the manual is to follow the form's numbering (A(1)–A(19), B(1)–B(7), C, D, then Nursing). Put the item ID on the policy that satisfies it, so the reviewer can match each box to a page. The form has no numbers for the seven Nursing items. I labeled them Nursing-1 to Nursing-7 in the order the form lists them. These seven items cite specific Medication Training and Technical Procedures (MTTP) sections, so the medication policies should reference those sections. The DDA Qualified Provider Application (Provider Application 9.19.25) says that if DDA approves the application, the policies and procedures must be submitted to OHCQ within 30 days of approval. The A(8) and A(9) wording on the form is shorter than the regulation's. A(8) says 'MATP' on the form. The regulation refers to the Administration's curriculum on medication training. COMAR 10.22.02.10 sets no separate policy about staff training. Staff training is a separate DDA checklist, 'Staff Training – DDS (COMAR 10.22.02.11C&D)', which is also marked DH Form DD.APP.1.1 (02/18). It is a training-record form, not a policy list, so I left it out of the items. The regulation text I used for sub-items is the current version on regs.maryland.gov.
